free_tier.stated: No storage quota at all. 16 GB per file via the Odysee uploader (4 GB from the plain lbry.com web form). Unlimited claims. Storage cost is a one-time LBC claim deposit, minimum 0.0001 LBC.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free. Files are content-addressed blobs served by the LBRY DHT/reflectors and by Odysee's CDN; retrieval by hash is not metered.

tooling: yt-dlp `lbry` extractor (verified present). Odysee JSON-RPC at api.na-backend.odysee.com (`resolve`, `claim_search`). LBRY Desktop hosts blobs locally under lbrynet/blob.
chaining: Unlimited claims per channel x unlimited channels x unlimited accounts. Because the object is a plain blob, there is no video-duration ceiling to fight — the only cap is 16 GB/file, so capacity = unlimited files x 16 GB.
limits_note: 16 GB per file is the real ceiling; no per-day upload cap documented. Every publish needs an LBC deposit, so a large library costs a real (small) crypto balance up front and must be re-staked to keep claims alive.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: This is the only candidate here that stores the original bytes, but the platform is visibly decaying in 2026 — community 'collapse watch' posts and a Sept 2026 outage report; LBRY Inc. wound down. Treat as a live archive with a short expected half-life.
